chapters.title: How does THIS give you internet?
chapters.narration: Your next click could go to space. Here is how Starlink makes that happen.

chapters.title: First stop: your terminal.
chapters.narration: Your router sends the request to this flat outdoor terminal. Its radio beam reaches a satellite moving overhead.

chapters.title: Steer the waves. Not the dish.
chapters.narration: Under the surface, antenna elements shift their timing. Their waves combine into a beam that follows a satellite, while the panel stays still.

chapters.title: A router in orbit.
chapters.narration: A few hundred kilometres up, the satellite receives and routes your data. Solar arrays power its electronics. Optical terminals reach other satellites.

chapters.title: Across space by laser.
chapters.narration: Some traffic crosses oceans and remote regions through laser links. Radio then carries it down to a ground gateway.

chapters.title: Back to the internet.
chapters.narration: The gateway connects to networks on Earth. Your reply travels back through the system.

chapters.title: Moving satellites. Changing links.
chapters.narration: Satellites keep moving, so your connection changes between them. Clear sky at the terminal still matters.

chapters.title: Try the interactive version.
chapters.narration: Open the satellite and steer the beam yourself at How Things Click.
